about: Every paragraph the result page can show. `bands` holds one paragraph per god for each band that config/scoring.json marks `describe: true`; if a band has no paragraph the next weaker one is used. `neglected` is shown for the god opposite the lead. `tiers` opens the page; placeholders {lead}, {second}, {leadPole} and {secondPole} are filled in.

tiers.clear: {lead} leads clearly. Of the seven polarities this is the one where your answers set you furthest from the middle, so it is likely to be what other people notice first. {second} comes next and gives it its manner.
tiers.clearAlone: {lead} leads clearly and stands alone: on the other six polarities your answers stay near the middle. Expect this one trait to explain most of what people notice about you.
tiers.shared: {lead} and {second} share the lead. Your answers put them within a step of each other, so read both as yours. Which one shows first tends to depend on the setting.
pantheios: Your answers sit near the middle on all seven polarities, so no single god leads. The result has a name of its own: Pantheios, “of all the gods”.

A balanced profile is a real pattern. People with it adapt to the setting: they can take charge or hold back, plan or improvise, press a point or let it go, and they are seldom the most extreme person in the room on anything. The gift is range. The risk is being hard to read, sometimes for yourself as well.

Two checks are worth making. If you chose the middle answer for most statements, take the test again and commit wherever a statement is even slightly more or less true of you than of others. Then look at the leanings below: they show which gods you favour when you favour any.

zeus.lean: You lean toward taking the lead. When a group drifts, you are more likely than most to say what should happen next, though you can sit back when someone else has it in hand. The pull shows mostly when nothing has been decided yet.
zeus.clear: Command is a settled part of how you work. You take the chair without being asked, set the terms, hand out roles and feel answerable for the outcome, and people tend to look to you for the decision. The cost is patience: being led, or waiting for agreement, wears on you faster than it wears on most.
zeus.strong: You run things. Deciding, directing and answering for the result is where you are most yourself, and others usually let you. At this strength the gift and its excess sit close together: protection turns into control, and confidence into the expectation that your word ends the discussion. What gets least room is Hades’ side, the plans and people that do better unmanaged and unseen.

hades.lean: You lean toward keeping things to yourself. You would rather watch a room than hold it, and you share a plan once it is ready. You can step forward when it matters, and you feel no need to do it otherwise.
hades.clear: Reserve is a settled part of you. You keep your own counsel, work out of sight and let results speak later, and you neither need an audience nor quite trust people who do. Others often find out late how much you were carrying. That protects your work, and it also means help and credit arrive late.
hades.strong: You live mostly below the surface. Your inner world is the real one, your plans and opinions stay yours until you choose otherwise, and applause means little to you. That depth is rare and steadying. At this strength it also becomes distance: people close to you can feel shut out, and decisions about you get made by those willing to speak. Zeus’ side, stepping up and saying it in the open, is the one you use least.

hermes.lean: You lean toward the new. Given a familiar route and an untried one, you are a little more likely than most to take the untried, and you pick up fresh interests easily. You still keep a base to return to.
hermes.clear: Roaming is a settled part of you. You learn fast, collect interests, and connect people and ideas that had not met. You are good at beginnings and at translating between worlds, and you get bored where nothing changes. Routine and long follow-through cost you more effort than they cost others.
hermes.strong: Novelty is your element. You are quick, curious and hard to pin down, and you would rather open five doors than furnish one room. This makes you inventive and well connected. At this strength it can also make you restless and a little slippery: commitments get traded for the next interesting thing, and a clever answer stands in for a true one. Hestia’s side, staying put and tending what you already have, gets the least of you.

hestia.lean: You lean toward the familiar. You like your places, your people and your routines, and you would rather improve what works than replace it. A good reason can still move you.
hestia.clear: Dwelling is a settled part of you. You keep the same ground for years and draw calm from it, and other people draw calm from you. You are where they left you, which makes you the centre things return to. Change for its own sake strikes you as noise, so you may wait too long before accepting a change that is needed.
hestia.strong: You are the fixed point. Continuity, routine and a kept home matter more to you than anything new on offer, and your steadiness holds other people’s lives together. At this strength the same constancy can harden into refusal: the world narrows to what is already known, and chances pass because taking them would disturb the order. Hermes’ side, going out to see what else there is, gets the least of you.

apollo.lean: You lean toward order. You like a plan and a clean finish, and loose ends bother you a little more than they bother most people. You can still improvise when the plan fails.
apollo.clear: Measure is a settled part of you. You plan ahead, hold to standards and finish the work before you play, and people rely on your results because you check them. The cost is ease: sloppiness, in yourself or in others, is hard for you to let pass, and you can find it difficult to enjoy what is merely good enough.
apollo.strong: You live by standards. Discipline, clarity and long preparation take you to a level most people do not reach, and you rarely miss what you aim at. At this strength the standard starts to rule you: flaws feel intolerable, rest feels unearned, and others meet your precision as coldness or judgement. Dionysus’ side, letting go and being carried by the moment, is the one you allow yourself least.

dionysus.lean: You lean toward the moment. You decide by feel a little more than by plan, and you loosen up easily in good company. When something has to be finished, you can still tighten up.
dionysus.clear: Release is a settled part of you. You follow mood and appetite, throw yourself fully into what you love, and bring a room to life. You work in bursts, often at your best close to a deadline. Schedules and delayed rewards feel like a cage, and things that need steady upkeep tend to slip.
dionysus.strong: You live for immersion. Music, company, sensation, work that takes you over: you want to disappear into it, and you take others with you. That intensity is a real gift and most people are glad of it. At this strength it also runs to excess: you overdo, forget what you promised, and leave the clearing up to someone else. Apollo’s side, the plan kept after the mood has gone, is the one you honour least.

aphrodite.lean: You lean toward keeping things pleasant. You notice how a remark will land and soften it a little, and on small matters you would usually rather agree than argue. You can still hold a line when it counts.
aphrodite.clear: Accord is a settled part of you. You read a room quickly, put people at ease, and get your way by drawing others toward you. People like being around you and cooperate more readily because of it. The cost is candour: you give way to protect the mood, and things that needed saying go unsaid.
aphrodite.strong: You are made for harmony. Charm, tact and a fine sense of what others want let you bring almost anyone round, and conflict rarely survives your presence. At this strength the wish to please starts to steer you: you say what will be welcome, avoid the fight you ought to have, and can lose track of what you want yourself. Ares’ side, saying it straight and risking the quarrel, is the one you use least.

ares.lean: You lean toward directness. You say what you think a little sooner than most people and you enjoy a contest. You can hold back when someone’s feelings are at stake.
ares.clear: Contest is a settled part of you. You speak plainly, like to win, and walk toward a conflict that others walk around. People know where they stand with you and are glad to have you on their side in a fight. The cost is friction: you can start arguments nobody needed and bruise people who were never opponents.
ares.strong: You are built for the fight. Courage, candour and force come naturally, and you are at your best when something has to be confronted. At this strength the fight starts to choose you: you escalate when pushed, compete over small things, and win the argument at the price of the relationship. Aphrodite’s side, winning people over by making it easy for them, is the one you use least.

athena.lean: You lean toward calm. Pressure rattles you a little less than it rattles most people, and you tend to think before you react. A hard enough day still gets through.
athena.clear: Composure is a settled part of you. Your voice and judgement stay the same when things go wrong, you sleep on decisions, and an insult does not hold your attention for long. People bring you their problems because you see them clearly. The cost is warmth: your calm can read as distance, and you may underrate how hard something is for those who feel it more.
athena.strong: You are very hard to shake. Under pressure you get cooler and more exact, you plan several moves ahead, and setbacks leave little mark. That makes you the person others want in a crisis. At this strength the control can turn against you: feelings get managed where they should be felt, and people who are less steady start to look merely weak. Poseidon’s side, being moved and letting it show, is the one you allow least.

poseidon.lean: You lean toward strong feeling. Things reach you a little faster and stay a little longer than they do for most people, and it usually shows. You still steady yourself fairly quickly.
poseidon.clear: Surge is a settled part of you. You feel things at full strength, your mood colours the day, and people rarely have to guess how you are. That makes you vivid, passionate and quick to sense what is wrong in a room. The cost is weather: bad days come in hard, and a slight can stay with you long after the other person has forgotten it.
poseidon.strong: Your feelings arrive like weather, and with the same force. Joy, anger, hurt and worry all come at full size, and they move the people around you too. This is where your power to care and to stir others comes from. At this strength it can also swamp you: decisions get made inside the storm, grudges outlast their cause, and others learn to brace. Athena’s side, the pause in which you cool down and think, is the one you reach least.

hera.lean: You lean toward commitment. Your people and your promises weigh a little more with you than your own plans do, and you like knowing where you belong. You still keep some ground of your own.
hera.clear: Bond is a settled part of you. You say “we”, keep your promises, remember the dates that matter, and stand up for your family or your organisation in front of outsiders. People can build on you. The cost is exposure: you can be let down badly, and disloyalty hurts you more than almost anything.
hera.strong: Your ties are the centre of your life. You commit fully, stay through the hard years, and build things that last because you do not leave. Few people are as dependable. At this strength the bond starts to hold too tightly: you watch for betrayal, keep score, and find it hard to forgive or to let someone go their own way. Artemis’ side, time and ground that belong to you alone, is the one you give yourself least.

artemis.lean: You lean toward independence. You need a bit more time on your own terms than most people do, and you are careful about what you sign up for. Close ties still matter to you.
artemis.clear: Freedom is a settled part of you. You keep your own ground and your own rules, need days alone to feel right, and avoid arrangements that leave you owing or answerable. You are self-reliant, clear about your limits, and quick to defend those who cannot defend themselves. The cost is closeness: people who want more of you often find the door half shut.
artemis.strong: You belong to yourself. Solitude restores you, obligation chafes, and you would rather do without than be managed or claimed. That independence gives you focus and a rare integrity. At this strength it also keeps people out: you leave before you can be held, punish a crossed boundary harder than it deserves, and can end up more alone than you meant to be. Hera’s side, the lasting tie that asks you to stay, is the one you grant least.

demeter.lean: You lean toward looking after people. You notice a little sooner than most when someone needs something, and helping comes easily. You can still leave people to manage on their own.
demeter.clear: Tending is a settled part of you. You see who has not eaten, who is struggling and who is ready for more, and you act on it. Teaching, feeding and raising others is the work that satisfies you most, and people grow around you. The cost is yourself: your own needs come last, and it is hard for you when those you raised stop needing you.
demeter.strong: You live to nourish. Other people’s needs and growth organise your days, and you give time, food and attention without counting. Many people owe you more than they know. At this strength care can close in: you help before you are asked, hold on when you should let go, and are left empty when the ones you tended move on. Hephaestus’ side, absorbing work on a thing that asks nothing back, is the one you give yourself least.

hephaestus.lean: You lean toward things over gatherings. A problem you can get your hands on holds you a little better than small talk does, and you like to fix what is broken. You still enjoy people in the right dose.
hephaestus.clear: Making is a settled part of you. You build, repair and refine, and you can lose hours in an object or a system without noticing. You show care by making something work for someone, and your results are solid because you stay with them. The cost is company: people can feel second to the project, and you may leave unsaid what the work was meant to say for you.
hephaestus.strong: The workshop is your home. You are happiest alone with a hard problem and good tools, and what you make is exact, inventive and built to last. Few people can match that concentration. At this strength the work becomes a hiding place: you answer feelings with fixes, let ties thin while you perfect a thing, and can grow bitter when the craft goes unnoticed. Demeter’s side, attention to the person in front of you, is the one you practise least.

neglected.zeus: Leading with reserve leaves Zeus short. His due is small and specific: say what you think before you are asked, take the decision that is yours to take, and let your work be seen while it can still be used.
neglected.hades: Leading with command leaves Hades short. His due is restraint: leave one decision to someone else, keep a plan to yourself until it is ripe, and spend time where nobody is waiting for your instructions.
neglected.hermes: Leading with dwelling leaves Hermes short. His due is one new thing at a time: a route you have not walked, a person outside your circle, a method you did not grow up with.
neglected.hestia: Leading with roaming leaves Hestia short. Her due is staying: finish one thing before starting the next, keep one ritual for a year, and go back to a place or a person when you would normally move on.
neglected.apollo: Leading with release leaves Apollo short. His due is a plan kept after the mood has passed: one schedule, one standard, one piece of work finished early and not rescued late.
neglected.dionysus: Leading with measure leaves Dionysus short. His due is time with no purpose and no score: music, a long table, anything you do badly and enjoy.
neglected.aphrodite: Leading with contest leaves Aphrodite short. Her due is making it easy for the other person: ask before you argue, grant the small point, and say the hard thing in a way that can be heard.
neglected.ares: Leading with accord leaves Ares short. His due is one honest disagreement: say the unwelcome thing plainly, let the mood suffer, and see that the tie survives it.
neglected.athena: Leading with surge leaves Athena short. Her due is the pause: a night’s sleep before the reply, the question of what you want to happen next, a plan made while the water is calm.
neglected.poseidon: Leading with composure leaves Poseidon short. His due is letting it land: admit that something hurt or mattered before you solve it, and let one person see you unsettled.
neglected.hera: Leading with freedom leaves Hera short. Her due is a promise that binds: let someone count on you, stay through a dull or difficult stretch, and accept help that leaves you in their debt.
neglected.artemis: Leading with bond leaves Artemis short. Her due is ground of your own: a day that answers to nobody, a pursuit that serves neither family nor firm, and the trust to let others go and come back.
neglected.demeter: Leading with making leaves Demeter short. Her due is attention to a person with nothing to fix: ask how they are and stay for the answer, teach what you know, eat with the others.
neglected.hephaestus: Leading with tending leaves Hephaestus short. His due is work that is only yours: a craft, a problem, an object you can lose an afternoon in while nobody needs you.

method: This is a short sorter: {count} statements, {perGod} for each god. It has not yet been tested on a sample of people, so the cut-offs are provisional and the result is a first reading, not a measurement.

Each polarity is scored as one god minus the other. If you are strong on both sides, as people often are on people against things, you land in the middle. Check the result against what two people who know you well would say.
